Button.purpose: A native button that triggers an action, with primary, secondary and ghost variants, tones, sizes, loading and policy-blocked states.
use: Use for any action that happens on the current page, such as save, run or confirm.
Use the primary variant for the single main action in a region.
Use blockedReason when policy forbids the action and the user needs to know why.

avoid.rule: Do not use a button with no visible text label.
Do not use a button to navigate to another page; render a link instead.
Do not place several primary buttons side by side.

keyboard.action: Activates the button.
Moves focus to the button; disabled and blocked buttons are skipped because they are natively disabled.

accessibility: While loading is true the button sets aria-busy and ignores clicks, and the spinner is hidden from assistive technology.
blockedReason disables the button and exposes the reason through the title attribute.
Icons passed as iconStart or iconEnd are wrapped in aria-hidden, so the text label must carry the meaning.

IconButton.purpose: A compact square button that shows only an icon, for familiar actions where space is tight.
use: Use for well-known actions such as close, more options or copy in toolbars and dense rows.
Pair with a Tooltip when the icon alone may be unclear to sighted users.

avoid.rule: Do not use for an action whose icon is not widely recognised.
Do not use as the main call to action of a page.

keyboard.action: Activates the button.

accessibility: aria-label is a required prop and a TypeScript error if missing; it is the button's only accessible name.
The icon is rendered aria-hidden, and while loading it is replaced by the spinner and the button sets aria-busy.
It inherits Button's disabled and blockedReason behaviour.

Card.purpose: A bordered surface that groups related content, either static or as a single clickable target.
use: Use a static card to group a short block of related content.
Pass href to make the whole card a link, or onClick to make it a button.
Use inside a CardGrid when showing several comparable items.

avoid.rule: Do not put buttons, links or inputs inside an interactive card; a development warning reports it.
Do not use a card as a large page section with its own heading structure.

keyboard.action: Follows the link when the card renders as an anchor with href.
Activates the card when it renders as a button with onClick.

accessibility: A static card renders as a div and does not receive focus.
An interactive card renders as a native a or button element, so its whole text content becomes the accessible name; keep it short.
Interactive cards show the shared focus ring on keyboard focus.

CardGrid.purpose: A layout wrapper that arranges Cards into a responsive grid.
use: Use to lay out a set of Cards of equal importance.
Use when the number of items varies and should wrap with the viewport.

avoid.rule: Do not use for tabular data that users compare across columns.
Do not use it to position arbitrary page regions.

accessibility: It renders a plain div with no role, so add a heading or a list structure yourself if the group needs one.
Tab order follows source order, so keep the card order meaningful.

Panel.purpose: A bordered container for a region of a page, rendered as a div, section or aside.
use: Use to frame a distinct region such as settings, a summary or a side note.
Set as to section or aside when the region has landmark meaning.

avoid.rule: Do not make a panel clickable; it has no interactive mode.
Do not nest panels deeply to create visual hierarchy.

accessibility: Choose as=section or as=aside to expose the matching element semantics.
Give a section panel a heading or aria-labelledby so the region has a name.

Badge.purpose: A small inline label for categories, counts or metadata, with tone styling and an optional icon.
use: Use for short metadata such as a version, a category or a count.
Use the tone prop to group related labels visually.

avoid.rule: Do not use for run or task status.
Do not use for the risk level of an operation.
Do not rely on tone colour alone to carry meaning; the text must say it.

accessibility: The optional icon is rendered aria-hidden, so the text is the accessible content.
A removable badge should use the cdt-badge__dismiss hook on a real button inside it; the consumer owns the remove behaviour and its label.

StatusBadge.purpose: Shows one of seven run or task statuses through colour, icon and text together.
use: Use for lifecycle states: queued, running, waiting, success, partial, danger and neutralEnd.
Pass the icon named by STATUS_ICONS for the status from the tokens package.

avoid.rule: Do not hide the label to show only the coloured icon; there is no icon-only mode.
Do not use for free-form categories.
Do not use for the risk of an action.

accessibility: status is limited to the seven typed values, and icon and label are required props.
The icon is aria-hidden and the label text provides the accessible name, so status is never conveyed by colour alone.
The rendered icon wrapper carries data-cdt-icon with the expected icon name.

SeverityTag.purpose: Marks the risk level of an operation as read, write, destructive or blocked, using colour, icon and text.
use: Use next to an action or permission to show how risky it is.
Pass the icon named by SEVERITY_ICONS for the severity from the tokens package.

avoid.rule: Do not use for the progress or outcome of a run.
Do not use for neutral metadata.

accessibility: severity, icon and label are required props.
The icon is aria-hidden and the label text carries the meaning, so severity is never colour alone.

Table.purpose: A styled native table with its own horizontal scroll container, for presenting rows of structured data.
use: Use for structured data that users scan and compare across columns.
Mark numeric cells with the numeric prop so figures align with tabular numerals.
Set aria-sort on a header cell to show the sort direction you control.

avoid.rule: Do not expect built-in sorting, pagination or virtual scrolling; the table is presentation only.
Do not use a table for page layout.

keyboard.action: Focuses the scroll container, which has tabIndex 0.
Scroll the focused container natively when the table overflows.

accessibility: Provide caption or aria-label; a development warning reports a table with neither.
Header cells default to scope=col.
The sort indicator drawn from aria-sort is excluded from the accessible name so it is not read twice.

Timeline.purpose: An ordered list of steps showing a sequence of events, with optionally selectable steps.
use: Use to show the ordered steps of a run or process.
Pass onSelect to a step to make it selectable, and selected to mark the current one.

avoid.rule: Do not use for unordered collections of items.
Do not use for multi-column records.

keyboard.action: Moves between steps that have onSelect; steps without it are not focusable.
Selects a step that has onSelect, which renders as a native button.

accessibility: The timeline renders as an ordered list, so step order is announced.
A selected step gets aria-current=step.
The step marker is aria-hidden, so the step text must describe the step.

CodeBlock.purpose: Displays a preformatted block of code or JSON in a monospace font with horizontal scrolling.
use: Use for multi-line code, configuration or JSON payloads.
Set language to record the language as a data attribute.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a single keyboard key or shortcut.
Do not expect syntax highlighting or a copy action built in.

keyboard.action: Focuses the code region, which has tabIndex 0.
Scroll the focused region natively when the code overflows.

accessibility: The wrapper has role=region and is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
Pass aria-label to name the region; the component does not set one itself.

Kbd.purpose: Renders a native kbd element to show a keyboard key or shortcut inline in text.
use: Use to show a key a user should press, such as Esc or Enter.
Use one Kbd per key in a key combination.

avoid.rule: Do not use for blocks of code or commands.
Do not use as a status or category label.

accessibility: It renders the native kbd element, which conveys keyboard input semantics.

Dialog.purpose: A modal window, built on Radix Dialog, for a focused confirmation or short task that blocks the page.
use: Use for a focused confirmation or short task that needs an answer before continuing.
Use for destructive confirmations where the user must stop and decide.

avoid.rule: Do not use for contextual detail the user wants to read alongside the page.
Do not use for a short hint or label.
Do not use for lightweight non-modal content anchored to a control.

keyboard.action: Opens the dialog from the focused trigger.
Moves focus between focusable elements inside the dialog; focus is trapped while open.
Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility: Include Dialog.Title so the dialog has an accessible name; Radix warns in development when it is missing.
Use Dialog.Description for supporting text; Radix links it to the dialog.
Radix traps focus, locks background scroll and restores focus on close.

Drawer.purpose: A side panel on the left or right, built on Radix Dialog, for contextual detail that keeps the page visible beside it.
use: Use for contextual detail that benefits from keeping the page alongside it.
Use for longer content such as a record inspector or a filter set.
Set side to left or right to match where the content belongs.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a short confirmation or decision.
Do not use for a small menu of actions.

keyboard.action: Opens the drawer from the focused trigger.
Moves focus between focusable elements inside the drawer; focus is trapped while open.
Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility: Include Drawer.Title so the drawer has an accessible name; Radix warns in development when it is missing.
It is modal: Radix traps focus, locks background scroll and restores focus to the trigger on close.

Tooltip.purpose: A short text label, built on Radix Tooltip, that appears on hover or keyboard focus of its trigger.
use: Use to name or briefly explain an IconButton or a truncated value.
Use when a StatusBadge or Badge needs more context in tight space.

avoid.rule: Do not put interactive content such as links or buttons in a tooltip.
Do not hide essential information only in a tooltip; touch users may never see it.
Do not use for long explanations.

keyboard.action: Focusing the trigger opens the tooltip.
Closes the open tooltip.
Closes the open tooltip.

accessibility: Wrap the app or region in Tooltip.Provider, which Radix requires.
The trigger must be focusable, such as a Button or IconButton, so keyboard users can reach the tooltip.
Radix links the content to the trigger with aria-describedby; it describes the trigger and does not replace an aria-label.

DropdownMenu.purpose: A menu of actions opened from a trigger, built on Radix Dropdown Menu, with optional icons and a danger tone.
use: Use to group secondary actions behind a single trigger, such as an IconButton for more options.
Use the danger tone on items that delete or cannot be undone.
Use Label and Separator to group related items.

avoid.rule: Do not use to choose a form value.
Do not use for free-form content or forms.
Do not hide the primary action of a page inside a menu.

keyboard.action: On the trigger, opens the menu and focuses the first item; on an item, activates it.
On the trigger, opens the menu; inside the menu, moves focus to the next item.
Moves focus to the previous item.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility: Radix sets the menu and menuitem roles and manages focus; do not override them.
Item icons are aria-hidden, so every item needs a text label.
A danger tone is visual only, so the item text must state the destructive action.

Popover.purpose: Non-modal floating content anchored to a trigger, built on Radix Popover, for small interactive panels.
use: Use for brief interactive content tied to a control, such as a small form or extra detail.
Pass container to portal into a locally themed region.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a plain text hint.
Do not use for a list of actions.
Do not use for a task that must block the page.

keyboard.action: Opens or closes the popover from the focused trigger.
Moves focus between focusable elements in the popover.
Closes the popover and moves focus to the trigger.

accessibility: Radix sets aria-expanded and aria-controls on the trigger and moves focus into the content on open.
Give the content a heading or aria-label when its purpose is not clear from the trigger.
Use Popover.Close for an explicit close button.

Field.purpose: Wraps a single form control with a label, optional description and error message, and wires them to the control.
use: Use around every TextField, TextArea, Select, Switch or Checkbox that needs a visible label.
Pass error to show a validation message and mark the control invalid.
Pass required to mark the field required on its control.

avoid.rule: Do not wrap more than one control in a single Field; it accepts exactly one child element.
Do not expect validation logic; Field only presents the state you pass.

accessibility: The label is linked to the control with htmlFor and id, and description and error are linked with aria-describedby.
An error sets aria-invalid on the control, so invalid state is not shown by colour alone.
The required asterisk is aria-hidden; the control itself receives required.

TextField.purpose: A single-line native text input with solid or glass variants, sizes, an optional leading icon and invalid styling.
use: Use for short free-text input such as a name, URL or search term.
Place inside a Field to get a label, description and error message.

avoid.rule: Do not use for multi-line text.
Do not use when the user must pick from a fixed set of options.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the input.
Moves the caret; typed characters enter text natively.
Submits the enclosing form, as a native input does.

accessibility: Provide a Field, aria-label or aria-labelledby; a development warning reports a missing label.
Invalid state sets aria-invalid, and the leading icon is aria-hidden.

TextArea.purpose: A multi-line native text area with solid or glass variants and invalid styling, defaulting to three rows.
use: Use for multi-line text such as descriptions, notes or prompts.
Place inside a Field to get a label, description and error message.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a single short value.
Do not use to display read-only code.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the text area.
Inserts a new line.

accessibility: Provide a Field, aria-label or aria-labelledby; a development warning reports a missing label.
Invalid state sets aria-invalid and links the error text through aria-describedby when inside a Field.

Select.purpose: A single-choice dropdown for form values, built on Radix Select, with a styled trigger and option list.
use: Use to choose one value from a short, fixed list of options.
Place inside a Field so the label, description, error and required state reach the trigger and the form control.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a long list that needs searching.
Do not use when several values can be chosen.
Do not use to trigger actions.
Do not use for a single on or off choice.

keyboard.action: On the trigger, opens the list and focuses the selected item; on an item, selects it and closes the list.
On the trigger, opens the list; inside the list, moves between items.
Closes the list and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility: Inside a Field the trigger gets the label link, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required.
Select.Root reads required from Field so the hidden form control also enforces it.
The selected-item check indicator is aria-hidden.

Switch.purpose: An on or off toggle, built on Radix Switch, for settings that take effect immediately.
use: Use for a binary setting that applies as soon as it changes.
Place inside a Field or give it an aria-label.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a choice that is only applied when a form is submitted.
Do not use for choosing among more than two options.

keyboard.action: Toggles the switch.

accessibility: Radix renders a button with role=switch and aria-checked.
Inside a Field it receives the label link, aria-describedby and aria-invalid from the Field.
Unlike TextField, it does not warn when no label is provided, so add one yourself.

Checkbox.purpose: A checkbox, built on Radix Checkbox, for selecting an option or agreeing to a statement.
use: Use for independent options in a form that are applied on submit.
Use for a single consent or acknowledgement.
Use the indicator prop to replace the default check glyph.

avoid.rule: Do not use for a setting that takes effect immediately.
Do not use for picking several values from a long list.

keyboard.action: Toggles the checkbox.

accessibility: Radix renders a button with role=checkbox and aria-checked.
Inside a Field it receives the label link, aria-describedby and aria-invalid; outside a Field, provide an aria-label or label.
The check indicator is aria-hidden.

Banner.purpose: Shows an inline page-level message in an info, warning or danger tone, with an optional title, icon and action.
use: Use it for persistent messages tied to the current page or section.
Use tone danger for failures and pass a recovery action in the action slot.

avoid.rule: Do not use it as a toast or snackbar; Conductor does not manage a notification queue.
Do not use it to explain why a list has no results.
Do not leave a danger banner without an action; development builds log a console warning.

accessibility: Tone danger renders role alert; info and warning render role status.
The icon slot is wrapped in aria-hidden, so the message text must carry the meaning.
Any focusable control in the action slot keeps its own keyboard behaviour.

EmptyState.purpose: Explains that an area has no content yet and offers an optional next step.
use: Use it when a list, table or panel has nothing to show.
Pass a description and an action when the user can fix the empty state.

avoid.rule: Do not use it while data is still loading.
Do not use it for a failed request that needs attention.
Do not present a failed or unknown result as zero results.

accessibility: The title prop is required and is rendered as text.
The icon is hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden.
It sets no live role, so announce changes elsewhere if needed.

Meter.purpose: Shows a measured value within a known range, such as quota or usage, with optional warning and exceeded thresholds.
use: Use it for a bounded quantity like storage or budget consumption.
Set warningAt and exceededAt to switch to the warning or exceeded tone.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for task progress toward completion.
Do not rely on the fill colour alone; always pass a meaningful valueText.

accessibility: Renders role meter with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext.
aria-label and valueText are required props.
The valueText is also shown visibly next to the track.

ProgressRing.purpose: Shows determinate progress toward a maximum as a compact ring with a visible text value.
use: Use it when the completed amount and the total are known.
Use size sm inside dense rows or cards.

avoid.rule: Do not use it when progress cannot be measured.
Do not invent a completion percentage without evidence.
Do not use it for a capacity or quota reading.

accessibility: Renders role progressbar with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext.
aria-label and valueText are required; valueText stays visible as the label.
The SVG ring is aria-hidden, and under reduced motion the text value carries the progress.

Spinner.purpose: Indicates indeterminate, in-progress work with an animated ring and a required text label.
use: Use it for short waits where progress cannot be measured.
Write a label that says what is loading.

avoid.rule: Do not use it when the amount of progress is known.
Do not use it as a placeholder for content layout.
Do not put it inside a button yourself; use the Button loading prop.

accessibility: Renders role status with aria-live polite.
The label prop is required; it is visually hidden but kept in the DOM.
Under prefers-reduced-motion the animation stops and the label becomes visible text.

Skeleton.purpose: Holds the place of content that is loading, with a required text label.
use: Use it where content will appear once a request finishes.
Give it a label that describes what is loading.

avoid.rule: Do not leave it in place after loading fails.
Do not use it when a request finished with no results.

accessibility: Renders role status with the label as its text.
The label prop is required.

AppShell.purpose: Provides the page frame with side navigation, an optional top bar, a skip link and a focusable main region.
use: Use it once per application as the outer layout.
Pass routeKey so a route change closes the mobile navigation and focuses main.
Place an AppShellNavTrigger in the top bar to open the navigation on narrow screens.

avoid.rule: Do not nest an AppShell inside another AppShell.
Do not use it for a side panel inside a page.

keyboard.action: The skip link is the first focusable element.
On the skip link, moves focus to the main region.
Closes the mobile navigation drawer.

accessibility: skipLinkLabel is required; navLabel names the mobile drawer and navCloseLabel names the scrim button.
The mobile drawer is a non-modal Radix Dialog; closing it returns focus to the opener, or to main after a route change.
The main region has tabIndex -1 so it can receive focus programmatically.

AppShellNavTrigger.purpose: The button that opens and closes the AppShell navigation drawer on narrow screens.
use: Place it inside AppShell, normally in the TopBar menuButton slot.
Use asChild to render it as an IconButton.

avoid.rule: Do not use it outside an AppShell.
Do not use it to open a general side panel.

keyboard.action: Toggles the navigation drawer.
Toggles the navigation drawer.

accessibility: It is a Radix Dialog trigger, so it carries aria-expanded and aria-controls for the drawer.
Give it an accessible name, especially when it shows only an icon.

NavList.purpose: Renders the primary navigation links with optional section labels, delegating link rendering to the consumer's router.
use: Use it for the main navigation inside AppShell.
Use renderLink to render your router's link component with the props it receives.
Mark the current item with active.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for in-page section switching.
Do not use it for a list of actions.
Do not use it for a location trail.

keyboard.action: Moves through the rendered links.
Follows the focused link.

accessibility: aria-label is required and names the nav landmark.
The active item receives aria-current page; spread the provided props onto your link.
Item icons are aria-hidden, so each item needs a text label.

TopBar.purpose: Shows the page header with an eyebrow, a title, action slots and an optional menu button slot.
use: Use it in the AppShell topBar slot.
Put the AppShellNavTrigger in menuButton and page-level actions in actions.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for navigation links.
Do not use it as a section heading inside page content.

accessibility: Renders a header element.
A string title is also set as the title attribute for truncated text.
Controls passed into the slots keep their own keyboard behaviour.

Tabs.purpose: Switches between related panels of content in the same place, built on Radix Tabs.
use: Use it for peer views of the same subject.
Keep the default manual activation when switching a panel is expensive.
Use forceMount on a panel whose state must survive switching.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for site navigation between pages.
Do not use it to show and hide a single section.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the tab list and then to the active panel.
Moves focus between tabs, skipping disabled ones.
Moves focus to the first or last tab.
Activates the focused tab in manual mode.

accessibility: Radix sets the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles, aria-selected and aria-controls.
Give Tabs.List an aria-label.
Activation is manual by default; with activationMode automatic, focusing a tab selects it.

Collapsible.purpose: Shows and hides one section of content behind a trigger, built on Radix Collapsible.
use: Use it for secondary detail that most users do not need at first.
Control it with open and onOpenChange when the state matters elsewhere.

avoid.rule: Do not use it to switch between several peer views.
Do not hide content that is required to complete the task.

keyboard.action: Opens or closes the content.

accessibility: Radix sets aria-expanded and aria-controls on the trigger.
Closed content is unmounted.
A disabled Collapsible ignores trigger activation.

Combobox.purpose: Lets the user type a query and pick one option from a filtered list, built on Downshift.
use: Use it to pick one value from a long or remote list.
Keep query and value separate and pass resultsQuery so stale results stay hidden.
Set state to loading or error while fetching.

avoid.rule: Do not use it when several values can be chosen.
Do not use it for a short, fixed list.

keyboard.action: Opens the list and moves the highlighted option.
Selects the highlighted option; ignored while IME composition is active.
Closes the option list.

accessibility: The label prop is required and is linked to the input by Downshift.
Downshift sets the combobox, listbox and option roles and the active option.
A status region announces loading, error and no-option states.

MultiSelect.purpose: Lets the user choose several options from a searchable checkbox group and shows the choices as removable chips.
use: Use it when several values can apply at once, such as filters.
Pass stable option ids; value holds the chosen ids.

avoid.rule: Do not use it when exactly one value is allowed.
Do not use it for a single on or off choice.

keyboard.action: Moves through the search field, chip remove buttons and checkboxes.
Toggles the focused checkbox.
On a chip remove button, removes that choice.

accessibility: Renders a fieldset with the label prop as its legend.
Each option is a Radix Checkbox inside a label.
Disabling the component disables the whole fieldset.

FilterChip.purpose: Shows one applied filter value with a button to remove it.
use: Use it to display active filters above results.
Group several chips in a FilterToolbar.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for a static status label.
Do not use it as a general action button.

keyboard.action: Activates the remove button.

accessibility: removeLabel is required and names the remove button.
Keep removeLabel specific, such as naming the value being removed.

FilterToolbar.purpose: Lays out filter controls and chips in a single wrapping row.
use: Use it to group FilterChip items and filter controls above a result set.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for page-level actions.

accessibility: It is a plain container with no role.
Controls inside keep their own keyboard behaviour.

DataTable.purpose: Displays loaded search results with externally controlled sorting, ID-based row selection, column visibility and load-more paging.
use: Use it for result sets that need sorting, row preview or incremental loading.
Sort in the parent or on the server and pass the sort state in.
Use state to show loading, error and partial results honestly.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for a small static table without these behaviours.
Do not expect it to sort rows; it only reports the requested order.

keyboard.action: Moves through sort buttons, row select buttons and the load more button.
Activates the focused button.

accessibility: label becomes the table caption; rowLabel names each row's select button.
Sorted columns get aria-sort, select buttons get aria-pressed and the root gets aria-busy while loading.
A status region reports how many rows are currently loaded.

WorkbenchLayout.purpose: Splits a results area from an optional inspector pane, with a slider to resize the inspector share.
use: Use it to show results next to a DetailInspector.
Pass onWidthChange to offer the non-drag width slider.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for the application frame.
Do not use it for a temporary overlay panel.

keyboard.action: On the width slider, adjust the inspector share.
On the width slider, jump to the minimum or maximum share.

accessibility: The width control is a native range input with a visible label.
The inspector share is clamped between 25 and 60 percent.

DetailInspector.purpose: Shows details of the selected item in a labelled region with a close button that returns focus to the selecting control.
use: Use it inside the WorkbenchLayout inspector slot to preview a selected row.
Pass returnFocusRef pointing at the control that opened it.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for a blocking task that needs a response.
Do not use it as a standalone overlay.

keyboard.action: Closes the inspector and returns focus to the returnFocusRef element.
On the close button, closes the inspector.

accessibility: Renders a section named by label, with label as a level two heading.
Focus returns without scrolling when it closes.

PathList.purpose: Shows a nested path tree where folders expand and leaf items can be selected.
use: Use it to browse a file or location hierarchy in a preview.
Mark items with state loading or error while their children resolve.

avoid.rule: Do not use it to show where the current page sits.
Do not use it for site navigation.

keyboard.action: Moves through folder summaries and leaf buttons.
Expands or collapses a folder, or selects a leaf.

accessibility: Folders use native details and summary elements.
Leaf buttons set aria-pressed for the selected item and are disabled without onPathSelect.
Loading and error states are announced through a status region.

Breadcrumb.purpose: Wraps a trail of links showing where the current location sits in a hierarchy.
use: Use it above content to show and link the parent locations.

avoid.rule: Do not use it as the primary navigation.
Do not use it to browse a whole tree.

accessibility: Renders a nav landmark with a default Korean aria-label; pass aria-label to rename it.
Links you place inside keep native link behaviour.

CopyButton.purpose: Copies a value to the clipboard and announces whether the copy succeeded or failed.
use: Use it next to an identifier, path or snippet the user is likely to paste elsewhere.

avoid.rule: Do not use it for a full code sample.
Do not use it for actions other than copying.

keyboard.action: Copies the value.

accessibility: A status region announces success, failure or that the clipboard is unavailable.
A late result for an old value is discarded when value changes.
The default label is Korean; pass label to change it.

RelationGraph.purpose: Shows a read-only graph of nodes and directed edges with an equivalent keyboard list and table of direction, state and evidence.
use: Use it to explore relations between items with their evidence.
Pass state to separate loading, empty, error and partial results.
Pass only data the viewer is allowed to see.

avoid.rule: Do not use it to edit, delete or create relations.
Do not read the layout as time order or dependency order.
Do not use it for plain tabular relations without a graph.

keyboard.action: Moves through the find field, type filter, list link, view buttons and the node and edge buttons.
On the list link, moves focus to the equivalent node list and table.
Activates the focused button to select a node or edge, zoom, pan or clear the selection.

accessibility: The SVG canvas is aria-hidden; every node and edge is reachable through the list and table.
label names the region and the table caption.
The selection detail region is aria-live polite, and the status line uses role alert on error.

ProcessingStatus.purpose: Lists each processing stage with its own status, detail and an optional consumer-provided action.
use: Use it to show receipt, storage, processing and indexing as separate stages.
Pass disabledReason when an action is not allowed.

avoid.rule: Do not treat receipt as index completion or overall completion.
Do not show a completion percentage or ETA without evidence.
Do not expect it to retry or poll on its own.

keyboard.action: Moves through stage action buttons.
Runs the focused stage action.

accessibility: Stages render as an ordered Timeline named by label.
Each status is shown as a text Badge, not by colour alone.
A blocked action is disabled and its reason is shown as visible text.
